review_candidates.title: Director
review_candidates.description: Company Description SUST Business Club is a student-led organization dedicated to fostering business knowledge, leadership, and professional development within the SUST community. The club organizes events such as workshops, competitions, seminars, and networking sessions that connect members with industry professionals and alumni. It provides a collaborative environment where students can develop practical skills in entrepreneurship, management, and communication. The club encourages inclusive participation from students of diverse academic backgrounds who are interested in business and leadership. Members gain hands-on experience through organizing initiatives and contributing to the club’s strategic growth. Role Description The Director role at SUST Business Club is a full-time, on-site position based in Sylhet. The Director will lead overall club operations, including planning and overseeing events, managing projects, and coordinating activities across different teams. This role involves setting strategic goals, supervising executive members, facilitating regular meetings, and monitoring progress on ongoing initiatives. The Director will also represent the club in communications with university authorities, partner organizations, and sponsors, ensuring professional and timely engagement. Day-to-day responsibilities include reviewing proposals, approving budgets, guiding marketing and outreach efforts, mentoring team members, and promoting an inclusive and collaborative culture within the club. Qualifications Candidates should possess strong leadership, team management, and decision-making skills to guide diverse groups and oversee multiple initiatives. Candidates should possess effective communication, public speaking, and interpersonal skills to represent the club and engage stakeholders. Candidates should possess organizational, time management, and project coordination skills to plan events and manage resources efficiently. Candidates should possess basic knowledge of business concepts, strategic planning, and problem-solving skills to support the club’s mission and growth. Candidates should possess networking and relationship-building skills to maintain partnerships with sponsors, mentors, and institutional bodies. Relevant experience in student organizations, event management, or leadership roles is beneficial. Familiarity with digital tools for communication, documentation, and promotion (e.g., office suites, social media platforms) is an advantage. Current enrollment at SUST and strong motivation to contribute to the student community are preferred.

review_candidates.title: Delivery Director
review_candidates.description: Symphony is a global design and development software company headquartered in San Francisco with 800+ technologists located across engineering offices in Southeast Europe and Latin America, along with business development offices in the US and Western Europe, and a Remote hub engaging employees from Latin America to Africa and Asia. In the last 20 years, we have launched over 400 products for the world’s leading startups, enterprises, Private Equity companies, and Fortune 500 companies. Our team has a proven track record in helping clients increase revenue, reduce time-to-market, improve end-user experiences, and achieve scalability. We have domain expertise spanning financial services, banking, retail, technology, healthcare, as well as the VC and PE ecosystem, among others. We are on the lookout for a Delivery Director. As a Delivery Director at Symphony, you will lead our client accounts and ensure clients achieve the results we promised. This is a value-led role, not a project management role: success means delivering results that clients recognise, not just delivering on time and within budget. You will lead AI-first delivery, ensure account profitability, and act as a trusted partner to client leaders. What would be your responsibilities if you join us? Agree with clients what success looks like, set clear measures and starting points, and track results against them. Present achieved results at quarterly business reviews, so clients can see the value and make clear decisions. Plan work around client goals rather than a feature list, and adjust the plan when priorities or dependencies change. Lead and grow the delivery team on your account, and build AI-first ways of working in delivery. Own the delivery side of the SOW: deliverables, acceptance criteria, assumptions and change control, and have renewals agreed before they expire. Forecast capacity, timelines and staffing for your accounts, and plan scenarios that keep client goals on track. Design and build AI workflows where AI and agents do real parts of analysis, engineering and QA, with clear review points and quality checks by people. Turn workflows that work into reusable practices, prompts and agent setups that other accounts can adopt. Use account data to show where AI saved time or cost, and where it did not. Manage quality, risks and dependencies, and escalate based on the impact on client goals. Protect account margin and price every scope change before agreeing to it. Spot and size new opportunities with clients, and pass qualified ones to our commercial team. Be a credible technical partner to client technology leaders, and explain technical trade-offs to non-technical stakeholders. There are some requirements that will make you stand out: Proven experience leading delivery of complex software projects for external clients at account level A track record of showing clients measurable business results, with examples you can walk us through. Experience with delivery forecasting, capacity and staffing planning. Hands-on experience designing, building and reusing AI workflows in delivery, not only using AI tools, and knowing when not to use AI. Good understanding of margin, pricing models (time and materials, fixed price, outcome-based) and proposals. Experience setting quality standards, managing risks and dependencies, and fixing the root causes of repeat problems. Enough technical knowledge of architecture, integrations and technical debt to be a credible peer to client CTOs. Strong communication, negotiation and stakeholder management skills with senior client leaders. Strategic thinking, ownership of results and the ability to lead teams through change. Fluent English, spoken and written. What this role offers you: Real ownership of your accounts. You own outcomes, scope and the SOW, and shape pricing together with our Senior Client Partner. You make the decisions on your account, not just coordinate them. Access to senior leaders from day one. You work directly with client CTOs and executives, including leaders at global consulting partners. Complex, multi-vendor delivery. Our largest accounts run alongside other vendors and consultancies, which builds experience you won't get on simpler projects. A real say in how AI-first delivery works. AI and agents already do real work on our projects. You help design the workflows, decide how they are governed and turn what works into practices other teams reuse. You will easily fit into Symphony culture if you: Are proactive and enthusiastic about your own continuous learning and improvement Have the ability to analyze and understand the business context and logic behind your job responsibilities Enjoy working in a pleasant and cooperative atmosphere Excited about working in international teams and using well-written and spoken English daily Ready to Join Us? We’re excited to hear from you! If this opportunity sparks your interest, don’t hesitate—let’s see where this journey can take us. We’ll review applications as they come in and promptly reach out to candidates chosen to move forward in the process. Curious to Learn More? If you have any questions our Talent Acquisition team is here for you. Feel free to drop us an email at ta@symphony.is. We’d love to connect! We may use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to support parts of the hiring process, such as reviewing applications, analyzing resumes, or assessing responses and identifying potential inconsistencies or verification signals in application materials based on available information. These tools assist our recruitment team but do not replace human judgment. Final hiring decisions are ultimately made by humans. If you would like more information about how your data is processed, please contact us.

review_candidates.description: Leadership is of utmost importance to us, not just as an add-on. Our expectations of our leaders and the entire Hellmann FAMILY are set out in our Leadership Principles. As a leader, you have a crucial role in perpetuating our culture, while also considering social, ecological, and economic sustainability. Check out the job details below! Purpose of the Position: The Country Head of Airfreight (CHAF) is responsible for the profitability, quality, performance, and growth of the Airfreight product in the Country. He/ She manages and is fully accountable for the Country Airfreight P&L down to CM2. He/ She acts in alignment with the CMD and works closely with Regional Airfreight and other products and functions within the Country, backed by globally aligned frameworks and concepts. Responsibilities: Implements a countrywide blueprint for Airfreight Operations, including centralization of selected activities/flows within a globally agreed framework. Functionally leads Airfreight Operations in Branches (Customer Service and Operational Service) Is accountable and responsible for Country Airfreight productivity, quality, and Customer Performance and takes corrective action where required. Ensures timely and accurate invoicing and job costing in country Airfreight Operations. Ensures country Airfreight operations are compliant with external regulations and internal policies (incl. e.g. Airfreight Safety and Security, DG qualifications, GDP compliance). Is consulted for and approves hiring into Airfreight positions in Branches. Develops new business jointly with CMD and Head of Sales. Directs efforts of Field Sales in alignment with Head of Sales. Develops and maintains relationships with major customers. Manages local Airfreight procurement and subcontractor performance and compliance in line with global carrier strategy and standards. Implements aligned global and regional Airfreight projects. Escalates to RHAF where conflicting top-down priorities inhibit meeting the above remit. Demonstrate full business ownership including P&L performance, forecast accuracy and timely corrective actions to close performance gaps. Apply fact-based and data-driven decision making and translate business information into clear recommendations and measurable actions. Demonstrate strong commercial acumen and build a close, constructive partnership with Country Sales. Previous Sales, Business Development or Commercial experience in freight forwarding is strongly preferred. Work jointly with Sales in identifying target customers, trade lanes and business opportunities, developing commercially competitive solutions while protecting sustainable GP and CM contribution. Bring solutions together with problems. Escalations should clearly state business impact, available options, recommendation and support required. Maintain proactive and transparent communication with the CMD, ensuring early escalation of material risks and avoiding preventable surprises. Translate agreed strategies and decisions into clear actions with ownership, milestones and measurable outcomes, ensuring disciplined follow-through to closure. Act with a Country-wide perspective and develop a strong organization through clear performance management, talent development and succession planning Target Metrics: Airfreight CM2 (=primary), Productivity, Tonnage Growth, Operational Quality, Customer Performance, Delivery of global/regional projects.

The company holds the highest share in the Egyptian cover switches market and exports to key Middle Eastern countries including KSA, Libya, Lebanon, Syria, UAE, Qatar, and Jordan. Customer safety is a top priority, and long-term client relationships reflect strong loyalty and trust in the brand. The company maintains an active presence on social media to engage with customers and showcase product developments. Role Description The Cost Accountant role at SAS For Electrical Industries is a full-time, on-site position based in 10th of Ramadan. The role is responsible for preparing, analyzing, and monitoring product and manufacturing costs, including standard costing, variance analysis, and cost allocation for materials, labor, and overhead. The Cost Accountant will support budgeting and forecasting, assist in the preparation and review of financial statements, and ensure accurate journal entries and account reconciliations. Daily tasks include tracking cost data, analyzing cost drivers, collaborating with production and procurement teams, and providing actionable cost insights to management. The role also involves maintaining compliance with internal controls and accounting policies, and contributing to continuous improvement in cost efficiency and profitability. Qualifications Candidates should possess strong skills in Cost Accounting and Finance to manage product costing, budgeting, and cost control activities. Candidates should possess the ability to prepare and interpret Financial Statements, ensuring accuracy and adherence to accounting standards. Candidates should possess Analytical Skills for cost analysis, variance investigations, and data-driven decision support. Candidates should possess proficiency in Journal Entries (Accounting) and account reconciliation to maintain accurate ledgers. Relevant qualifications such as a bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field; professional certifications (e.g., CMA) are an advantage. Strong proficiency in Excel and accounting/ERP systems; familiarity with manufacturing or industrial environments is preferred. Attention to detail, numerical accuracy, and the ability to work collaboratively with cross-functional teams on-site. Good written and verbal communication skills in English and Arabic, and the ability to meet deadlines in a fast-paced setting.

review_candidates.title: Controls Systems Integration Leader
review_candidates.description: Job Description Summary As a Controls Systems Integration Leader, you will play a key role in translating GE Vernova Wind Turbine product requirements into controls system requirements, developing controls parameter settings, and supporting the successful execution of critical New Product Introductions (NPIs). Reporting to the Controls Integration Leader, you will join a global team of systems engineers within the Controls Sub-System organization of GE Vernova Wind Engineering. In this highly collaborative role, you will work closely with Controls engineers, cross-functional subsystem teams, Systems Engineering, Product Line Management, and Services/Customer Engineering to ensure controls solutions are fully integrated, validated, and aligned with product and customer needs. Supporting multiple concurrent product development programs and an installed fleet of more than 40,000 wind turbines worldwide, you will have the opportunity to make a significant impact on the reliability, performance, and continuous improvement of GE Vernova's wind turbine technology. Your contributions will help accelerate the delivery of reliable, affordable, and sustainable energy solutions to customers around the globe. Job Description Roles and Responsibilities Develop and maintain Product Level Requirements (PLRs) and System Level Requirements (SLRs) for wind turbine Controls systems, ensuring alignment with overall product and system objectives. Collaborate with cross-functional engineering teams and functional owners to define, validate, and deploy turbine Controls parameter sets that support performance, reliability, safety, and operability requirements. Lead Controls integration activities for New Product Introductions (NPIs), driving execution of significant Controls work packages across all development phases, from concept and design through validation, certification, and product deployment. Ensure compliance with Controls Lifecycle Management processes, engineering standards, and Controls & Operability governance requirements. Support the investigation and resolution of product and fleet quality issues through root cause analysis, corrective actions, and continuous improvement initiatives related to Controls software and system performance. Prepare and deliver technical reports, design reviews, and presentations for internal and external stakeholders, including engineering leadership, customers, and cross-functional teams. Strong understanding of the product development lifecycle, including requirements development, system design, verification, validation, and product launch activities. Ability to manage multiple priorities and project deliverables, demonstrating strong organizational skills and attention to detail in a fast-paced development environment. Collaborate successfully within a multicultural, globally distributed engineering organization, building strong partnerships across functions, regions, and disciplines. Desired Characteristics Strong communication skills with the ability to simplify complex technical topics. Experience with system-level design and integration of complex products or control systems. Knowledge of real-time control systems, such as GE MarkVIe or similar platforms. Ability to translate customer and product needs into clear, testable technical requirements. Customer-focused mindset with the ability to balance short- and long-term priorities. Strong analytical, problem-solving, and cross-functional collaboration skills. For US Based Candidates Master's Degree from an accredited university or college in Engineering, STEM, or related field with 10+ years of relevant professional experience. 10 years experience in Controls, Systems, or Services engineering. 5 years experience in wind turbine engineering, product design, or technology development. For Spain Based Candidates Significant experience in Engineering/Technology & Controls Engineering. Knowledgeable level is comparable to a Master's Degree from an accredited university or college (or a high school diploma with relevant experience). Advanced English proficiency required. Eligibility Requirements For US based candidates, the required work location is GE Vernova in Greenville, SC. Candidates must be willing to work onsite at this location. For candidates outside of the United States, the required work location is GE Vernova in Barcelona, Spain. GE Vernova offers a great work environment, professional development, challenging careers, and competitive compensation. GE Vernova is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, national or ethnic origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, disability, protected veteran status or other characteristics protected by law. GE Vernova will only employ those who are legally authorized to work in the United States for this opening. Any offer of employment is conditioned upon the successful completion of a drug screen (as applicable). Relocation Assistance Provided: Yes For candidates applying to a U.S. based position, the pay range for this position is between $113,200.00 and $188,800.00. The Company pays a geographic differential of 110%, 120% or 130% of salary in certain areas. The specific pay offered may be influenced by a variety of factors, including the candidate’s experience, education, and skill set. Bonus eligibility: discretionary annual bonus.
